subject: math
title: Line Plots with Fractions: Totals and Fair Shares
seo_title: Grade 5 Line Plots with Fractions Worksheets: Unlike Denominators, Total of the Data and Redistribute Equally
standard_text: Make a line plot to display a data set of measurements in fractions of a unit (1/2, 1/4, 1/8). Use operations on fractions for this grade to solve problems involving information presented in line plots. For example, given different measurements of liquid in identical beakers, find the amount of liquid each beaker would contain if the total amount in all the beakers were redistributed equally.
meta_desc: Free Grade 5 line plot worksheets with fractions: read and make line plots in eighths, add and subtract with unlike denominators, find the total of the data with count × value, and redistribute equally (fair share) like the beaker problem. 100 practice questions with answers.
key_big: Total = each value × its number of X's, added up. Fair share = total ÷ number of X's.
key_sub: 8 beakers holding 3 liters in all: each would contain 3 ÷ 8 = 3/8 liter. Rename to a common denominator before adding or subtracting, and divide by the number of items, not the number of marks.
body_html:
What a line plot shows

A line plot is a number line with an X for each measurement. When a value repeats, the X's stack up. Mark the number line in eighths when the data has eighths, and label each mark in simplest form: 28 is 14, 48 is 12, 68 is 34.

A class poured water into 8 identical beakers. The amounts in liters are: 38, 18, 34, 14, 12, 18, 58, 14.

Find the total of all the data

Each X is one beaker. For each mark, multiply the number of X's by the value. Then add the results with a common denominator.

X'sValueCount × value
2 X's182 × 18 = 28
2 X's142 × 14 = 48
1 X381 × 38 = 38
1 X121 × 12 = 48
1 X581 × 58 = 58
1 X341 × 34 = 68
8 X's2 + 4 + 3 + 4 + 5 + 6 = 24 eighths = 3 liters

Redistribute equally

“If the water were shared equally” means: find the total, then divide by the number of items (the number of X's).

Example

If all the water were poured together and shared equally among the 8 beakers, how much water would each beaker contain?

Total: 3 liters. There are 8 beakers, so 3 ÷ 8 = 38.

Answer: 38 liter

Example

Another set of 4 beakers holds 12, 38, 38 and 34 liter. If the water were shared equally, how much would each beaker contain?

Total in eighths: 48 + 38 + 38 + 68 = 168 = 2 liters. Then 2 ÷ 4 = 24 = 12.

Answer: 12 liter

When the total is not a whole number, multiply by a unit fraction: 94 ÷ 8 = 94 × 18 = 932. Write every answer in simplest form.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Dividing by the number of marks (6)Divide by the number of X's (8 beakers)
Adding each value once: 18 + 14 + … Multiply each value by its number of X's first
Stopping at the total (3 liters)“Shared equally” means divide the total by the number of items
Adding the denominators: 12 + 38 = 410Rename first: 48 + 38 = 78
Reading 38 as 34Look at the bottom number: eighths are smaller than fourths
Using the ends of the number line as the greatest and leastUse the X's farthest to the right and left

faq.a: It asks students to make line plots of measurements in halves, fourths and eighths and to solve problems with the data using fraction operations, such as finding a total or sharing the total equally.

faq.q: How do you redistribute equally on a line plot?
faq.a: Find the total of all the measurements, then divide it by the number of items (X's). For 8 beakers holding 3 liters in all, each beaker would contain 3 ÷ 8 = 3/8 liter.

faq.q: How do you find the total of the data on a line plot with fractions?
faq.a: Multiply each value by the number of X's above it, then add the results using a common denominator. Four X's at 3/8 give 4 × 3/8 = 12/8 = 1 1/2.

faq.q: How is the 5th grade line plot standard different from 4th grade?
faq.a: In 4th grade students add and subtract fractions with like denominators from a line plot. In 5th grade they also use unlike denominators, multiplication and division, such as sharing a total equally.

sets.title: Read a line plot in eighths

items.q: Zoe measured 9 leaves. The line plot shows the lengths. How many leaves are 2 inches long?
items.e: Find 2 on the number line. Count only the X's in that column: 3.

items.q: Hana measured 14 frog jumps. The line plot shows the jump lengths. Which jump length is the most common?
items.e: The most common value has the tallest stack of X's. The stack above 3 14 has 4 X's, more than any other.

items.q: Mr. Diaz's class measured some pencils. The line plot shows the lengths. How many pencils are shown on the line plot?
items.e: Each X is one pencil. Add the X's in every column: 3 + 2 + 2 + 1 + 2 = 10.

items.q: Eli cut 15 pieces of ribbon. The line plot shows the lengths. How many pieces are 128 yards long?
items.e: The marks are labeled in simplest form. 128 = 1 12, so look at the mark labeled 1 12. Count the X's above it: 5.

items.q: Chloe recorded the rainfall for 15 days. The line plot shows the rainfall amounts. How much rain fell on the wettest day?
items.e: Look for the X that is farthest to the right: it is above 1. The mark 1 18 has no X above it.

items.q: Mrs. Patel's class weighed 16 rocks. The line plot shows the weights. How many rocks weigh 78 pound?
items.e: Find 78 on the number line. Count only the X's in that column: 2.

items.q: Jack filled 14 bags of trail mix. The line plot shows the weights. How many bags hold more than 78 pound of trail mix?
items.e: Count only the X's to the right of 78. Do not count the X's above 78 itself. Add the X's to the right: 3 + 4 = 7.

items.q: Omar cut 16 pieces of yarn. The line plot shows the lengths. How long is the shortest piece?
items.e: Look for the X that is farthest to the left: it is above 1 14. The first mark, 1 18, has no X above it.

items.q: Max filled 10 jars with sand. The line plot shows the weights. What fraction of the jars hold 78 pound of sand? Write it in simplest form.
items.e: There are 10 X's in all, and 2 of them are above 78. So the fraction is 210 = 15.

items.q: Kai measured the heights of 12 bean plants. The line plot shows the heights. How many bean plants are 228 inches tall?
items.e: The marks are labeled in simplest form. 228 = 2 34, so look at the mark labeled 2 34. Count the X's above it: 2.

items.q: Ruby measured 13 leaves. The line plot shows the lengths. Which length is the most common?
items.e: The most common value has the tallest stack of X's. The stack above 3 has 4 X's, more than any other.

items.q: Sofia measured some frog jumps. The line plot shows the jump lengths. How many jumps are shown on the line plot?
items.e: Each X is one jump. Add the X's in every column: 3 + 4 + 3 + 2 + 3 + 1 = 16.

items.q: Mr. Kim's class poured water into 10 identical beakers. The line plot shows the amounts. What fraction of the beakers hold 58 liter of water? Write it in simplest form.
items.e: There are 10 X's in all, and 2 of them are above 58. So the fraction is 210 = 15.

items.q: Luis poured juice into 12 glasses. The line plot shows the amounts. How much juice is in the fullest glass?
items.e: Look for the X that is farthest to the right: it is above 1 18. The mark 1 14 has no X above it.

items.q: Ms. Brown's class checked 15 cans of leftover paint. The line plot shows the amounts. How many cans hold 28 gallon of paint?
items.e: The marks are labeled in simplest form. 28 = 14, so look at the mark labeled 14. Count the X's above it: 4.

items.q: Ava measured 13 pencils. The line plot shows the lengths. How many pencils are longer than 4 78 inches?
items.e: Count only the X's to the right of 4 78. Do not count the X's above 4 78 itself. Add the X's to the right: 2 + 4 + 1 = 7.

items.q: Maya cut 16 pieces of ribbon. The line plot shows the lengths. How long is the shortest piece?
items.e: Look for the X that is farthest to the left: it is above 1 58. The first mark, 1 12, has no X above it.

items.q: Ms. Brown's class recorded the rainfall for 15 days. The line plot shows the rainfall amounts. How many days had 34 inch of rain?
items.e: Find 34 on the number line. Count only the X's in that column: 3.

items.q: Mia weighed 12 rocks. The line plot shows the weights. What fraction of the rocks weigh 1 38 pounds? Write it in simplest form.
items.e: There are 12 X's in all, and 3 of them are above 1 38. So the fraction is 312 = 14.

items.q: Ms. Brown's class filled 14 bags of trail mix. The line plot shows the weights. How many bags hold 1 18 pounds of trail mix?
items.e: Read the labels carefully: 1 18 and 1 14 are different marks. Find 1 18 and count the X's above it: 4.

sets.title: Make a line plot from data

items.q: Ben weighed 8 rocks. The weights in pounds are: 1 78, 1 78, 1 78, 1 34, 2, 2, 1 12, 1 38. Ben made this line plot but forgot one X. Where does the missing X go?
items.e: Count how many times each value is in the list. 1 38 is in the list once, but the plot has no X above it. The missing X goes above 1 38.

items.q: Lily measured the heights of 9 bean plants. The heights in inches are: 2 34, 2 58, 2 38, 2 12, 2 34, 2 12, 3, 2 38, 2 34. Lily made this line plot but forgot one X. Where does the missing X go?
items.e: Count how many times each value is in the list. 3 is in the list once, but the plot has no X above it. The missing X goes above 3.

items.q: Grace measured 10 frog jumps. The jump lengths in feet are: 2 12, 2, 3, 2 14, 2 12, 2, 2 12, 2 14, 2 14, 2. Grace made this line plot but forgot one X. Where does the missing X go?
items.e: Count how many times each value is in the list. 2 is in the list 3 times, but the plot shows only 2 X's above it. The missing X goes above 2.

items.q: Ms. Brown's class filled 8 jars with sand. The weights in pounds are: 1 14, 1 18, 34, 1 38, 1 38, 1 38, 1 14, 1 18. The class made this line plot but forgot one X. Where does the missing X go?
items.e: Count how many times each value is in the list. 1 14 is in the list 2 times, but the plot shows only 1 X above it. The missing X goes above 1 14.

items.q: Sam poured water into 9 identical beakers. The amounts in liters are: 78, 58, 12, 58, 34, 12, 12, 34, 1 18. Sam made this line plot but forgot one X. Where does the missing X go?
items.e: Count how many times each value is in the list. 34 is in the list 2 times, but the plot shows only 1 X above it. The missing X goes above 34.

items.q: Ms. Lee's class cut 8 pieces of ribbon. The lengths in yards are: 1 78, 2 14, 1 78, 148, 1 34, 1 78, 2, 148. The class makes a line plot marked in eighths, with each mark labeled in simplest form. How many X's go above 1 34?
items.e: 148 = 1 34, so both go above the same mark. In the list, 1 34 appears once and 148 appears 2 times: 1 + 2 = 3 X's.

items.q: Mr. Diaz's class measured 10 beetles. The lengths in inches are: 1, 48, 58, 58, 34, 78, 12, 34, 34, 1. The class makes a line plot marked in eighths, with each mark labeled in simplest form. How many X's go above 12?
items.e: 48 = 12, so both go above the same mark. In the list, 12 appears once and 48 appears once: 1 + 1 = 2 X's.

items.q: Mrs. Patel's class checked 8 cans of leftover paint. The amounts in gallons are: 28, 12, 14, 38, 28, 38, 28, 34. The class makes a line plot marked in eighths, with each mark labeled in simplest form. How many X's go above 14?
items.e: 28 = 14, so both go above the same mark. In the list, 14 appears once and 28 appears 3 times: 1 + 3 = 4 X's.

items.q: Ms. Brown's class measured 7 leaves. The lengths in inches are: 3 14, 3, 3 18, 228, 2 34, 228, 2 78. The class makes a line plot marked in eighths, with each mark labeled in simplest form. How many X's go above 2 34?
items.e: 228 = 2 34, so both go above the same mark. In the list, 2 34 appears once and 228 appears 2 times: 1 + 2 = 3 X's.

items.q: Nora made this line plot. Then she added one more value: 268 inches. Above which mark should she draw the X?
items.e: 268 = 3 14 (divide the top and bottom by 2). The mark is labeled 3 14, so the X goes there.

items.q: Leo made this line plot. Then he added one more value: 148 pounds. Above which mark should he draw the X?
items.e: 148 is more than 1: 8 eighths make 1 whole, so 148 = 1 68 = 1 34. The X goes above 1 34.

items.q: Owen made this line plot. Then he added one more value: 208 inches. Above which mark should he draw the X?
items.e: 208 = 2 12 (divide the top and bottom by 4). The mark is labeled 2 12, so the X goes there.

items.q: Noah made this line plot. Then he added one more value: 228 feet. Above which mark should he draw the X?
items.e: 228 is more than 1: 8 eighths make 1 whole, so 228 = 2 68 = 2 34. The X goes above 2 34.

items.q: Zoe weighed 7 apples. The weights in pounds are: 12, 34, 38, 1, 58, 34, 78. She wants a line plot with a mark for every weight. How should the number line be marked?
items.e: Some weights, like 38 and 58, are eighths of a pound. Halves and fourths have no mark for them, so the number line must be marked in eighths.

items.q: Hana measured 6 leaves: 1 12, 1 34, 2 14, 2, 2 12, 1 78 inches. She makes a line plot marked in fourths: 1 12, 1 34, 2, 2 14, 2 12. Which length has no mark on this line plot?
items.e: A fourths scale only has marks at 0, 14, 12, 34, 1 and so on. 1 78 is an eighth, so it falls between two marks. The line plot needs to be marked in eighths.

items.q: Eli measured 6 shells: 34, 12, 1 14, 1, 38, 34 inches. He makes a line plot marked in fourths: 14, 12, 34, 1, 1 14. Which length has no mark on this line plot?
items.e: A fourths scale only has marks at 0, 14, 12, 34, 1 and so on. 38 is an eighth, so it falls between two marks. The line plot needs to be marked in eighths.

sets.title: Add and subtract with unlike denominators

items.q: Chloe recorded the rainfall for 16 days. The line plot shows the rainfall amounts. How much more rain fell on the wettest day than on the driest day?
items.e: Greatest: 1 18. Least: 14. Write them with denominator 8: 1 18 = 98, 14 = 28. Subtract: 98 − 28 = 78 inch.

items.q: Jack measured the heights of 14 bean plants. The line plot shows the heights. How much taller is the tallest bean plant than the shortest bean plant?
items.e: Greatest: 2 14. Least: 1 12. Use the X's, not the ends of the number line. Write them with denominator 4: 2 14 = 94, 1 12 = 64. Subtract: 94 − 64 = 34 inch.

items.q: Omar measured 16 beetles. The line plot shows the lengths. How much longer is the longest beetle than the shortest beetle?
items.e: Greatest: 1 12. Least: 34. Write them with denominator 4: 1 12 = 64. Subtract: 64 − 34 = 34 inch.

items.q: Max poured water into 15 identical beakers. The line plot shows the amounts. How much more water is in the fullest beaker than in the beaker with the least water?
items.e: Greatest: 78. Least: 14. Use the X's, not the ends of the number line. Write them with denominator 8: 14 = 28. Subtract: 78 − 28 = 58 liter.

items.q: Kai cut 16 pieces of ribbon. The line plot shows the lengths. How much longer is the longest piece than the shortest piece?
items.e: Greatest: 2 12. Least: 1 34. Write them with denominator 4: 2 12 = 104, 1 34 = 74. Subtract: 104 − 74 = 34 yard.

items.q: Ruby filled 12 bags of trail mix. The line plot shows the weights. How much more trail mix is in the fullest bag than in the bag with the least?
items.e: Greatest: 1 18. Least: 12. Use the X's, not the ends of the number line. Write them with denominator 8: 1 18 = 98, 12 = 48. Subtract: 98 − 48 = 58 pound.

items.q: Sofia cut 13 pieces of yarn. The line plot shows the lengths. Find the greatest value and the least value on the line plot. What is their sum?
items.e: Greatest: 1 34. Least: 78. Write them with denominator 8: 1 34 = 148. Add: 148 + 78 = 218 = 2 58 yards.

items.q: Luis measured 11 beetles. The line plot shows the lengths. Find the greatest value and the least value on the line plot. What is their sum?
items.e: Greatest: 1 38. Least: 12. Write them with denominator 8: 1 38 = 118, 12 = 48. Add: 118 + 48 = 158 = 1 78 inches.

items.q: Ava poured water into 15 identical beakers. The line plot shows the amounts. Find the greatest value and the least value on the line plot. What is their sum?
items.e: Greatest: 1 18. Least: 12. Write them with denominator 8: 1 18 = 98, 12 = 48. Add: 98 + 48 = 138 = 1 58 liters.

items.q: Mrs. Patel's class poured juice into 16 glasses. The line plot shows the amounts. What is the difference between the most common amount and the smallest amount?
items.e: Most common: 58 (the tallest stack). Smallest: 14. Write them with denominator 8: 14 = 28. Subtract: 58 − 28 = 38 cup.

items.q: Maya recorded the rainfall for 16 days. The line plot shows the rainfall amounts. What is the difference between the most common rainfall amount and the smallest rainfall amount?
items.e: Most common: 78 (the tallest stack). Smallest: 12. Write them with denominator 8: 12 = 48. Subtract: 78 − 48 = 38 inch.

items.q: Mia filled 16 bags of trail mix. The line plot shows the weights. What is the difference between the most common weight and the lightest weight?
items.e: Most common: 34 (the tallest stack). Lightest: 12. Write them with denominator 4: 12 = 24. Subtract: 34 − 24 = 14 pound.

items.q: Ben checked 14 cans of leftover paint. The line plot shows the amounts. What is the difference between the most common amount and the smallest amount?
items.e: Most common: 12 (the tallest stack). Smallest: 14. Write them with denominator 4: 12 = 24. Subtract: 24 − 14 = 14 gallon.

items.q: Lily weighed 14 rocks. The line plot shows the weights. How much greater is the greatest value than the most common value?
items.e: Greatest: 1 12. Most common: 1 14 (the tallest stack). Write them with denominator 4: 1 12 = 64, 1 14 = 54. Subtract: 64 − 54 = 14 pound.

items.q: Grace measured 15 leaves. The line plot shows the lengths. How much greater is the greatest value than the most common value?
items.e: Greatest: 3 18. Most common: 2 34 (the tallest stack). Write them with denominator 8: 3 18 = 258, 2 34 = 228. Subtract: 258 − 228 = 38 inch.

items.q: Mrs. Patel's class poured juice into 16 glasses. The line plot shows the amounts. How much greater is the greatest value than the most common value?
items.e: Greatest: 1 18. Most common: 12 (the tallest stack). Write them with denominator 8: 1 18 = 98, 12 = 48. Subtract: 98 − 48 = 58 cup.

items.q: Sam measured 6 beetles. The lengths in inches are: 34, 1 38, 12, 1 58, 1 14, 78. What is the difference between the greatest and the least value?
items.e: Find the greatest, 1 58, and the least, 12. Do not just use the first and last numbers in the list. Write them with denominator 8: 1 58 = 138, 12 = 48. Subtract: 138 − 48 = 98 = 1 18 inches.

items.q: Emma cut 6 pieces of ribbon. The lengths in yards are: 1 34, 1 18, 2 12, 1 12, 2 18, 2 14. What is the difference between the greatest and the least value?
items.e: Find the greatest, 2 12, and the least, 1 18. Do not just use the first and last numbers in the list. Write them with denominator 8: 2 12 = 208, 1 18 = 98. Subtract: 208 − 98 = 118 = 1 38 yards.

items.q: Theo's leaves are shown on a line plot. The greatest value is 34 inch more than the least value. The least value is 2 14 inches. What is the greatest value?
items.e: “More than” means add. Write them with denominator 4: 2 14 = 94. Add: 94 + 34 = 124 = 3 inches.

items.q: Nora's rocks are shown on a line plot. The greatest value is 1 12 pounds more than the least value. The least value is 58 pound. What is the greatest value?
items.e: “More than” means add. Write them with denominator 8: 1 12 = 128. Add: 58 + 128 = 178 = 2 18 pounds.

items.q: Leo measured 15 pencils. The line plot shows the lengths. What is the total length of all the pencils that are 4 58 inches long?
items.e: There are 2 X's above 4 58. Multiply: 2 × 4 58 = 2 × 378 = 748. 748 = 9 14. The total is 9 14 inches.

items.q: Mr. Kim's class cut 14 pieces of yarn. The line plot shows the lengths. What is the total length of all the pieces that are 1 38 yards long?
items.e: There are 2 X's above 1 38. Multiply: 2 × 1 38 = 2 × 118 = 228. 228 = 2 34. The total is 2 34 yards.

items.q: Mrs. Green's class recorded the rainfall for 14 days. The line plot shows the rainfall amounts. What is the total rainfall on all the days that had 1 18 inches of rain?
items.e: There are 3 X's above 1 18. Multiply: 3 × 1 18 = 3 × 98 = 278. 278 = 3 38. The total is 3 38 inches.

items.q: Owen filled 16 jars with sand. The line plot shows the weights. What is the total weight of the sand in all the jars that hold 1 38 pounds of sand?
items.e: There are 3 X's above 1 38. Multiply: 3 × 1 38 = 3 × 118 = 338. 338 = 4 18. The total is 4 18 pounds.

items.q: Noah measured 14 leaves. The line plot shows the lengths. What is the total length of all the leaves that are 3 34 inches long?
items.e: There are 3 X's above 3 34. Multiply: 3 × 3 34 = 3 × 154 = 454. 454 = 11 14. The total is 11 14 inches.

items.q: Mrs. Green's class weighed 16 rocks. The line plot shows the weights. What is the total weight of all the rocks that weigh 58 pound?
items.e: There are 5 X's above 58. Multiply: 5 × 58 = 258. 258 = 3 18. The total is 3 18 pounds.

items.q: Eli measured 9 frog jumps. The line plot shows the jump lengths. What is the total length of all the jumps?
items.e: Multiply each value by its number of X's: 1 × 1 58 = 1 58, 1 × 1 34 = 1 34, 3 × 1 78 = 3 × 158 = 458, 4 × 2 = 8. Add them with denominator 8: 138 + 148 + 458 + 648 = 1368 = 17 feet.

items.q: Mrs. Patel's class poured juice into 8 glasses. The line plot shows the amounts. What is the total amount of juice in all the glasses?
items.e: Multiply each value by its number of X's: 1 × 38 = 38, 2 × 12 = 22 = 1, 3 × 58 = 158, 2 × 34 = 64. Add them with denominator 8: 38 + 88 + 158 + 128 = 388 = 4 34 cups.

items.q: Chloe cut 9 pieces of ribbon. The line plot shows the lengths. What is the total length of all the pieces?
items.e: Multiply each value by its number of X's: 1 × 58 = 58, 1 × 34 = 34, 3 × 78 = 218, 4 × 1 = 4. Add them with denominator 8: 58 + 68 + 218 + 328 = 648 = 8 yards.

items.q: Jack cut 8 pieces of yarn. The line plot shows the lengths. What is the total length of all the pieces?
items.e: Multiply each value by its number of X's: 1 × 1 12 = 1 12, 1 × 1 34 = 1 34, 2 × 1 78 = 2 × 158 = 308, 4 × 2 = 8. Add them with denominator 8: 128 + 148 + 308 + 648 = 1208 = 15 yards.

items.q: Mr. Diaz's class recorded the rainfall for 9 days. The line plot shows the rainfall amounts. What is the total rainfall on all the days?
items.e: Multiply each value by its number of X's: 1 × 34 = 34, 2 × 78 = 148, 3 × 1 = 3, 3 × 1 18 = 3 × 98 = 278. Add them with denominator 8: 68 + 148 + 248 + 278 = 718 = 8 78 inches.

items.q: Omar filled 9 jars with sand. The line plot shows the weights. What is the total weight of the sand in all the jars?
items.e: Multiply each value by its number of X's: 1 × 1 38 = 1 38, 1 × 1 12 = 1 12, 5 × 1 58 = 5 × 138 = 658, 2 × 1 34 = 2 × 74 = 144. Add them with denominator 8: 118 + 128 + 658 + 288 = 1168 = 14 12 pounds.

items.q: Mrs. Patel's class measured 6 leaves. The line plot shows the lengths. What is the total length of all the leaves?
items.e: Multiply each value by its number of X's: 3 × 1 12 = 3 × 32 = 92, 2 × 1 58 = 2 × 138 = 268, 1 × 1 78 = 1 78. Add them with denominator 8: 368 + 268 + 158 = 778 = 9 58 inches.

items.q: Max weighed 9 rocks. The line plot shows the weights. What is the total weight of all the rocks?
items.e: Multiply each value by its number of X's: 3 × 34 = 94, 2 × 78 = 148, 2 × 1 = 2, 2 × 1 18 = 2 × 98 = 188. Add them with denominator 8: 188 + 148 + 168 + 188 = 668 = 8 14 pounds.

items.q: Mrs. Green's class measured 15 beetles. The line plot shows the lengths. What is the total length of the beetles that are longer than 78 inch?
items.e: Use only the X's to the right of 78, not the X's above 78. Multiply each value by its number of X's: 3 × 1 = 3, 2 × 1 18 = 2 × 98 = 188. Add them with denominator 8: 248 + 188 = 428 = 5 14 inches.

items.q: Kai checked 12 cans of leftover paint. The line plot shows the amounts. What is the total amount of paint in the cans that hold more than 38 gallon of paint?
items.e: Use only the X's to the right of 38, not the X's above 38. Multiply each value by its number of X's: 2 × 12 = 22 = 1, 1 × 58 = 58, 1 × 34 = 34. Add them with denominator 8: 88 + 58 + 68 = 198 = 2 38 gallons.
